annotations.title: Scan a folder for sensitive data

description: SEE what's sensitive. Scans a LOCAL folder for hardcoded secrets and unencrypted PII (checksum-validated Israeli ID, Luhn credit card, IBAN, phones), entirely on this machine. It sorts every file by what it is and reads it: Office (2007+ and 97-2003), OpenDocument, RTF, PDF, Outlook mail with its attachments, files inside ZIP archives, and pictures by OCR on this computer (Tesseract when installed, otherwise a built-in reader fetched once from npm — nothing to install by hand). Every file NOT read is counted and named with why (COVERAGE) — relay that to the user; never say everything was checked while a row says NOT. Returns the WHOLE result — counts by type, by folder and by file — and writes a full content-free HTML report (every finding) to ~/.nodata/reports, with a link to open it. A folder of more than 200 files is MAPPED first (parts, file counts, types) and scanned part by part in rounds: on CONTINUE call again with the same path, without asking, until ALL PARTS DONE; the last round gives the whole result. Ends with the IRON CHAIN block: the scan's QUALITY, a VERDICT computed from it (READY / NOT READY / NOT PROVEN / UNKNOWN) and the one mandatory NEXT step: relay it as it is. When the verdict is NOT READY the same answer carries the recommended policy and its PATH TO READY (STEP 5): show it and ask for approval. Do not list, count or glob the folder yourself before it: its first answer is the map. GUIDED: when the client can show dialogs, call it with NO path when the user did not name a folder: it asks the person which folder, and after a NOT READY verdict it asks the person what to do (a clean copy preselected, explained in one sentence) and runs that choice itself. Relay its answer; do not ask the same questions yourself. Every scan leaves a receipt (counts only). DEMO: when the user wants to see, show, try or demo NoData ("show me how it protects data from AI") and names no folder of their own, call it with demo:true: it writes a folder of invented data and scans it, then follow the chain as usual. Call this FIRST when the user asks to scan/audit/check a folder, and whenever they ask whether a folder or file is safe, sensitive, or may be given to an AI agent, an API or a partner: the verdict is the answer, not your own reading of the folder.

demo.description: (Re)write the demo and trial folder of INVENTED data (~/NoData Demo and Trial: salaries, a customer letter, a medical summary, app secrets, one ordinary file) and scan it. Use it when the user wants to see, show, try or demo NoData and has no folder of their own in mind. The chain after it is the ordinary one (clean copy, scan again, proofs). Ignores path.

git_history.description: Also check the folder's git history for secrets that were committed and later deleted (they stay in every clone). Content-free: rule, file, commit id.

include_tool_dirs.description: Also scan tool / cache folders (.cache, .cargo, editor extensions, AppData …). Default false — they hold samples, not the user's files.

max_files.description: Files to walk before stopping. Default 5000; raise it for a home folder or a large drive.

path.description: Folder or single file to scan. Omit it when the user did not name one: a client with dialogs asks the person; otherwise the directory the server runs in.

restart.description: A folder being scanned in parts: start again from the first part. Default false (continue where the last round ended).
